posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked: In each iteration, sleep 100 & starts a background job. The condition (( i % 2 )) || kill % kills the most recent background job only when i is evem, since (( i % 2 )) fails in that case. Thus, all even-numbered sleeps are killed, and only the odd ones survive. Finally, 6 background processes remain.

posts.name: S.Vignesh
posts.cooked:
I think it is the opposite in the case of arithmetic expansion. For zero value, the condition (( )) will fail and for non zero value (( )) will be successful. So, the sleep process will be killed on even iterations leaving only the odd jobs alive at the end of the for loop.
